paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The Teacher tells the young man to rejoice, to let his heart be glad, and he never says joy is a problem. He also says God will bring him to judgment for all these things (Ecclesiastes 11:9). So the Teacher's point isn't to be gloomy. It's to enjoy your days with your eyes open, because youth and vigor are fleeting (Ecclesiastes 11:10).

Then comes the line the whole passage leans on: "Remember your Creator in the days of your youth…" (Ecclesiastes 12:1). Notice the deadline. The days of adversity are coming, and the Teacher paints them as a house going dim and quiet, with a silver cord snapped and a golden bowl crushed (Ecclesiastes 12:6). I think he paints it so clearly because he wants you to hear him NOW, not later. Later is a very popular day on the calendar, and it never once showed up to bake a single batch.

So what do you do with it today, baker? You don't wait until things get dark to turn toward God. You remember Him while the oven is warm, because the dust returns to the ground, and the spirit returns to God who gave it (Ecclesiastes 12:7). The Teacher's last word is that everything is futile (Ecclesiastes 12:8). That tells me anything we pile up without our Creator won't hold, so start with Him today.
